purpose: Investigate, without feedback, whether the different nonconditioning spatial memories present in the raw-two and fused sequence-23 trajectories can change the same-frame decoded mask. Both full-video runs used the same initial automatic prompt and matched spatial/pointer key counts; their later trajectories may differ.
scope: Previously inspected cropped seq23 frames 8,20,35,48,51, already fixed in the earlier same-read fusion study. Engineering uses saved seq3 reads at 8 and 12. This is post-hoc selected analysis, not an independent efficacy test.
capture: Reproduce the archived raw-two trajectory with the original one-time initialization and a read-only snapshot observer; require masks and all memory/position traces to match. Reuse the previously verified unchanged fused snapshots. Sequence 23 excludes the inset before the detector and encoder. No later redetection or new threshold/gate.
intervention: At a given frame, independently reproduce each snapshot's no-op attention and decoder. Require equal spatial and pointer counts, identical current image query, query positions, high-resolution image features, conditioning memory and conditioning positions. Swap the entire nonconditioning spatial feature and position segment between raw-two and fused reads while preserving each recipient's own conditioning keys, pointer keys/values, current query and decoder image features. Thus counts and pointer values match each recipient's no-op. This swaps multiple memories, temporal positions and trajectory-derived content together; it is not a selective fusion ablation or a deployable policy.
verification: First independently repeat raw-two seq3 captures, then validate both saved reads and cross-swaps on seq3 in two fresh processes. Verify exact no-op, parameter identity, query/condition equality, spatial and pointer sizes, position alignment and recipient pointers. Repeat seq23 cross-swaps independently, freeze outputs before labels, and independently rescore masks. Report present Dice, empty false alarms, pre-swap key counts and per-frame outcomes.
interpretation: Differences are conditional same-frame counterfactuals between different propagated memories; memory entries and timestamps change together while pointer tails remain recipient-specific. They cannot isolate fusion, frame count, object-pointer contribution, later feedback or independent generalization. All frames and sequences are previously inspected.
